I live in a home with a dappled shade yard, and will be living here long term (4+ years). The front bed has no grass, but has azaleas, peonies, camellias, and a few yuccas toward the street where there’s a bit more sun. The soil is clay where I live, zone 8b. The layer of topsoil is gone in many places, leaving red clay at the surface. Amending the soil to create a wooded understory garden would mean bringing in and tilling material in this fall after the heat breaks, bringing mulch in the spring and then being able to plant.

Or, I could spend my time and labor collecting an assortment of pots and create a lovely container garden, but I’d still probably put a layer of mulch down over the bare dirt. If I leave after 4 years, I could take my favorites with me.

My gardening has been primarily a large collection of orchids and a hydroponic system that grows herbs and cherry tomatoes, so I feel confident I could do some really great container gardening, but there’s a lot to be said for growing in the ground, even if it would be a bit silly to improve the soil on land I don’t own.
